docs.title: The mathematical anchor
docs.text:
For the specific operator definitions and assumptions in Evgeny's Theorem, the fourth-moment trace defect is

\[ \Delta_m(H^4,\theta) = \mathrm{Tr}(H_C^4)-\mathrm{Tr}(H_{C'}^4) = -16(3^{m-1}+1)\sin^2\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right), \qquad m\geq 1. \]

With the documented normalization, the intensive invariant is

\[ I_m(\theta) = \frac{\Delta_m(H^4,\theta)}{3^{m+1}+3} \longrightarrow -\frac{16}{9}\sin^2\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right). \]

At theta = pi/2, the limiting value is -8/9. The primary repository reports a Lean 4 proof for the concrete formalized operators and its stated quantifiers. This does not prove higher moments, physical laws, quantum advantage, or runtime invariants.

measure → state → invariant gate → allowed transition → execute → verify

It reports a 10,000-km vehicle/energy-system scenario under a deliberately high 1,500 Wh/kg pack-level energy-density research sweep. The README reports 2.761 MWh for a baseline scenario, 3.205 MWh for an adverse scenario, and 2.716 MWh for a bounded-controller hypothesis. docs.title: 4. RFT-Cosmology-Genesis
docs.text:
The source repository records a reproducible Pass-1 phenomenological calculation using the stated invariant

\[ I_m(\theta)=-16\frac{3^{m-1}+1}{3^{m+1}+3}\sin^2\!\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right), \qquad q_m=1+\epsilon I_m(\theta). \]

The repository now has a proposed analytic statement for the exact limit and finite-level remainder:

\[ I_\infty(\theta)=-\frac{16}{9}\sin^2\!\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right), \qquad I_m(\theta)-I_\infty(\theta) =-\frac{32}{9(3^m+1)}\sin^2\!\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right). \]

The theorem document and regression tests are being reviewed in the source repository's PR #1. The source PR's CI has passed, but human review and merge remain pending. This hub treats the statement as an analytic result under review, not as a merged release or Lean-formalized theorem.

The cosmology repository itself explicitly limits its scope: the coupling is phenomenological; the acoustic calculation is reduced; baseline acoustic multipoles are reference values; and no full CMB likelihood is implemented. No observational detection, new physical law, or physical origin for \(\epsilon\) is claimed.

  • Primary source: RFT-Cosmology-Genesis
  • Model specification: MODEL_SPEC.md
  • Limitations: LIMITATIONS.md
  • Theorem review: PR #1

docs.title: 5. Evidence and claim boundaries
docs.text:
Use these labels consistently across the programme:

  • Formal theorem: a proposition proved in a specified formal system for its exact definitions and assumptions.
  • Numerically reproduced: a computational result tied to named code, inputs, parameters, tolerances, and outputs.
  • Engineering-tested: a claim supported by tests or experiments for a specified implementation and configuration.
  • Research architecture: a proposed design whose key physical or operational requirements remain to be validated.
  • Modelled scenario: an output of a model under declared assumptions; not a physical measurement.
  • Patent-oriented disclosure: technical material organized for counsel review; not a statement of patent grant, patentability, priority, or freedom to operate.

A successful test suite, an attractive banner, a numerical fit, or a patent-oriented document cannot by itself promote a claim to a stronger evidence category. Report unresolved validation items rather than silently treating them as complete.

docs.text:
Primary sources: source repository, theorem statement, Lean formalization, and verification record.

docs.title: 2. Evgeny's Theory of Everything: higher-moment recurrence programme
docs.text:
Primary sources: repository, dissertation, final status, and claims and evidence.

This programme studies trace defects for higher even moments \(H^6\), \(H^8\), and \(H^{10}\), including Fourier-coefficient candidates, exact finite-level modular/CRT certificates, and independent sparse-matrix numerical holdouts. The repository reports checks through level 7 for specified finite sets of angles and a pinned Lean build for the upstream fourth-moment result. These are distinct evidence types. The universal all-level higher-moment recurrence remains open: finite certificates and numerical agreement do not establish it.

docs.title: 3. Phi-Genesis: signed-flux spectral analysis
docs.text:
Primary sources: repository, verified results, research map, and reproducibility guide.

Phi-Genesis investigates signed \(\mathbb{Z}_2\)-flux graph Laplacians on Sierpiński-gasket approximations, spectral decimation, spectral gaps, boundary/corner corrections, inertia-based counting, and exploratory integer mass-index patterns. The factor-5 decimation structure is reported with boundary/corner qualifications. Gate A remains open because the full exceptional set and all residual mismatches have not been explained. The proposed index set \(\{1,12,17,40\}\) is not established as a predictive selection law. The signed-flux operators are not assumed equivalent to the SU(2)-connected operators in Evgeny's Theorem.

docs.title: 5. SIRM engineering architecture
docs.text: SIRM is the Synthetic Intelligence Reasoning Model. In the engineering repositories, the operational core is a state-transition model constrained by explicit invariants, arithmetic checks, permission boundaries, and reproducible tests. These implementation-level constraints must be documented and verified against the actual code. They are not consequences of the spectral trace identity unless a separate formal connection is stated and proved.

docs.title: 4.1 Methodology
docs.text:
We constructed a discrete-event simulation that models GreedyScheduler behavior under controlled contention patterns. The simulation is not a production validator measurement — it is a reference model designed to isolate and observe scheduling behavior under specific workload assumptions.

Simulation parameters: - Priority queue (max-heap by compute_unit_price) - Thread-aware account locks (write/read conflict detection) - Per-pass execution model: scheduled transactions hold locks for one pass, then release - Incoming traffic: 50 tx per scheduling pass - Worker threads: 4 - Drain passes: 200+ after input stops

docs.text: No verification method can exhaustively prove absence of bugs. docs.title: Field Trial: seL4 Capability Derivation Tree Stress-Verification
docs.text: Document ID: RFT-EXP-SELC4-2026-001 Date: 2026-08-03 Laboratory: RFT-SIRM / UltraCore-RFT Classification: Reproducible Research Artifact Revision: Final

docs.title: Abstract
docs.text:
This report documents a deterministic empirical verification experiment in which the UltraCore-RFT stress-testing methodology was applied to the Capability Derivation Tree (CDT) of the seL4 microkernel. The experiment executed more than one billion pseudo-random, syntactically valid capability operations under deterministic seed control. No kernel crashes, panics, or allocator-level invariant violations were observed during the monitored execution. The seL4 test suite completed successfully after the marathon phase.

Disclaimer: This experiment does not claim to prove, improve, or replace the formal verification of seL4. It records only observable, reproducible behavior under sustained load.

docs.title: 1. Objective
docs.text:
To empirically observe the stability and resource reclamation behavior of the seL4 CDT implementation when subjected to a sustained sequence of valid capability invocations generated by a deterministic, seed-controlled pseudo-random process.

Working Hypothesis:

Under a deterministic pseudo-random sequence of syntactically valid capability invocations, the seL4 CDT implementation does not produce kernel panics, unrecoverable page faults, or VKA-level memory leaks detectable by the test harness.

This hypothesis is empirically falsifiable and does not constitute a mathematical theorem about seL4 correctness.

docs.title: 6. Relationship to UltraCore-RFT
docs.text:
This experiment demonstrates that the deterministic empirical verification methodology developed within UltraCore-RFT / SIRM is transferable from the blockchain runtime layer to the operating-system layer.

The SIRM core methodology:

  1. Deterministic seed control — every state transition sequence is reproducible
  2. Invariant telemetry — quantitative metrics recorded after every batch
  3. Resource drain verification — system must return to a known clean state
  4. Complementary checking — empirical stress runs operate alongside formal specifications

The object of study is not seL4 itself, but the applicability of the methodology.

docs.title: 7. Research Contribution
docs.text: # Contribution Description 1 Deterministic empirical stress verification Seed-controlled, reproducible protocol for sustained pseudo-random valid load 2 Repeatable capability verification methodology Documented procedure: build → run → drain → measure 3 Complementary verification alongside formal proofs Empirical layer checking runtime invariants without asserting specification coverage 4 CI-ready kernel regression methodology Lightweight harness integrable into CI pipelines 5 Reusable research framework Single-file drop-in module for sel4test, adaptable to custom extensions

docs.title: 8. Limitations
docs.text:
1. Empirical, not mathematical. This experiment provides observational data. It does not constitute a formal proof of seL4 correctness, nor does it replace the existing Isabelle/HOL proof.
  2. Valid-input only. Only syntactically correct, ABI-compliant invocations were used. Malformed system calls, invalid capability encodings, and kernel binary fuzzing were excluded.
  3. Limited object coverage. Only Endpoint, Notification, and TCB objects were retyped. Page tables, ASID pools, frames, IRQ control, and device untypeds were not tested.
  4. Single-threaded. No concurrency, inter-CPU races, or multi-process capability transfers were exercised.
  5. Emulated hardware. QEMU virt was used. Timing, cache behavior, and memory-ordering effects on physical silicon may differ.
  6. Observational ceiling. A zero-fault result over 10⁹ operations does not imply that the 10⁹+1-th operation cannot fail. It is a statistical sample, not an exhaustive enumeration.

docs.title: Core Invariants
docs.text: The SIRM (Stable Invariant Resource Model) defines four hard constraints that every RFT-SIRM system must satisfy after every state-mutating operation.

docs.title: I1: Supply Conservation
docs.text:
total_supply = total_base_sum + global_field * p

Where: - total_supply — total economic supply in the system - total_base_sum — sum of all individual base balances - global_field — uniform scalar shift applied to all participants - p — number of active participants

The total supply is decomposed into a uniform field component (global_field * p) and individual deviations (total_base_sum). This decomposition enables O(1) redistribution.

docs.title: I2: Mint/Burn Accounting
docs.text:
total_supply = total_minted - total_burned

Supply is strictly derived from minted and burned amounts. No implicit inflation or deflation paths exist.

docs.title: I3: Dust Bound
docs.text:
dust_accumulator < p (when p > 0)

Dust (rounding remainder from division operations) is bounded by participant count. When p decreases (unregister), dust is re-normalized to maintain the bound.

docs.title: I4: Debt Limit
docs.text:
effective_balance[i] >= -(total_supply / 10p)

Where effective_balance[i] = base_balance[i] + global_field.

No participant can accumulate debt beyond a fraction of total supply. The factor of 10 is a protocol parameter.

docs.title: Standard Model
docs.text:
In typical distributed systems, distributing a reward R to p participants requires:

for i in 0..p:
    balance[i] += R / p    -- O(p) operations

At p = 1,000,000, this is 1,000,000 storage writes.

docs.title: RFT Model
docs.text:
In RFT-SIRM, distribution is a single scalar update:

global_field += R / p    -- O(1) operation

All participants' effective balances increase by R / p simultaneously because effective_balance[i] = base_balance[i] + global_field.

This is a different mathematical model, not an optimization.

docs.title: Effective Balance
docs.text:
effective_balance[i] = base_balance[i] + global_field
  • base_balance[i] — individual deviation from the uniform field
  • global_field — shared scalar shift

docs.title: Transfer with Edge Cost
docs.text:
// From sender
delta_from = amount + edge_cost
base_balance[from] -= delta_from

// To receiver
delta_to = amount
base_balance[to] += delta_to

// Edge cost handling
if edge_cost > 0:
    // Burn: reduce total supply
    total_supply -= edge_cost
elif edge_cost < 0:
    // Mint: increase total supply
    total_supply += |edge_cost|

Edge cost is a protocol-level mechanism for directed taxation or subsidization.

docs.title: Negative Entropy
docs.text:
// Deflationary tick
global_field -= e * 10^18  // where e is Euler's number

// Compensate total_base_sum to preserve I1
total_base_sum += e * 10^18 * p

This creates deflationary pressure on effective balances while preserving the supply invariant.

docs.title: Evgeny's Theorem: An Exact Spectral Identity
docs.text: Unlike the operational analogies above, this section states a concrete mathematical result about a concrete object. It is independent of the runtime modeling language used elsewhere in this document. Source, tests and data: RFT-SIRM/Evgeny-Theorem.

docs.title: Object
docs.text:
SG(m) is the Sierpiński-gasket graph at refinement level m, with n(m) = (3^(m+1) + 3) / 2 vertices and 3^m elementary triangles. The Hilbert space is C^n ⊗ C². Every edge carries an SU(2) unitary, and flux is injected through one designated edge per triangle. Two configurations are compared at the same angle θ:

  • C (non-commuting): the rotation axis cycles x / y / z by triangle index, so holonomies of neighbouring triangles genuinely do not commute.
  • C′ (commuting control): the axis is fixed to z, which is exactly two decoupled U(1) copies.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Δ_m(H⁴, θ) = Tr(H_C⁴) − Tr(H_C′⁴) = −16 · (3^(m−1) + 1) · sin²(θ/2)

Normalizing by dim(H) = 3^(m+1) + 3 gives the intensive invariant I_m(θ), which converges to −(16/9) · sin²(θ/2). At θ = π/2 the limit is exactly −8/9.

m dim(H) Δ_m(H⁴, π/2) I_m(π/2) 1 12 −16 −1.333333 3 84 −80 −0.952381 5 732 −656 −0.896175 7 6,564 −5,840 −0.889701

The defect vanishes exactly for the moments p = 1, 2, 3 and first appears at p = 4, so a single gauge-invariant spectral moment separates a non-Abelian connection from its commuting control.

docs.title: Verification Status
docs.text: Statement Status The closed form matches direct computation for every tested (m, θ), m = 1…7 (held-out pairs, θ-grid, level 7) Established (reproducible) The fourth moment is gauge-invariant under random SU(2) gauge transformations Established (spectrum change ≤ 8 × 10⁻¹⁵) The closed form holds for all m ≥ 1 and θ Machine-checked in Lean 4 (concrete operators, fourth moment; no sorry, standard axioms only) Lean 4 formalization Complete for the stated scope (formalization/README.md); independent review of the formal definitions pending

docs.title: Scope and Limits
docs.text:
• The closed form applies strictly to the fourth moment. It is not a statement about the full spectrum, the spectral gap, or any other moment.
  • It is not a physical theory, and it does not address the Yang–Mills existence-and-mass-gap problem or any other Millennium Prize Problem.
  • Relationship to SIRM: the two share a methodology (state the invariant first, then test it at every scale, with held-out checks). There is currently no mathematical derivation connecting the theorem to the runtime invariants I1–I4.

docs.title: 2.1 Evgeny's Theorem — fourth-moment trace-defect identity
docs.text:
Primary source: Evgeny-Theorem · Theorem statement · Lean formalization · Verification record.

For the concrete operator definitions and assumptions in the source project, the fourth-moment trace defect is stated as

\[ \Delta_m(H^4,\theta) =\mathrm{Tr}(H_C^4)-\mathrm{Tr}(H_{C'}^4) =-16(3^{m-1}+1)\sin^2\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right), \qquad m\geq1. \]

The source repository reports a Lean 4 formalization. This status applies to that specific proposition and its formal definitions; it does not prove the higher-moment recurrence, the Phi-Genesis decimation criterion, SIRM runtime invariants, or a cosmological interpretation.

docs.title: 2.2 Evgeny's Theory of Everything — higher moments and synthesis
docs.text:
Primary source: Evgeny's Theory of Everything · Dissertation · Final status · Claims and evidence ledger.

This synthesis track investigates recursive graph operators, Fourier coefficients, residuals, and candidate recurrence relations for moments \(H^6\), \(H^8\), and \(H^{10}\). Exact modular/CRT certificates cover specified finite-level coefficient claims, and independent sparse-matrix calculations provide finite numerical holdouts. The all-level recurrence remains open; finite certificates and numerical agreement must not be presented as an all-level proof.

docs.title: 2.3 Phi-Genesis — signed-flux spectral research
docs.text:
Primary source: Phi-Genesis · Research map · Verified results · Reproducibility guide.

Phi-Genesis studies signed \(\mathbb{Z}_2\)-flux Laplacians on Sierpiński-gasket graph approximations, spectral decimation, spectral gaps, boundary/corner corrections, inertia, and candidate integer mass-index patterns. The factor-5 decimation structure is reported with boundary/corner qualifications. Gate A remains open: the full exceptional set and residual mismatches are not completely characterized. The proposed index set \(\{1,12,17,40\}\) has not been established as a predictive selection law. This operator family is distinct from the SU(2)-connected operators in Evgeny's Theorem unless and until a precise bridge is proved.

docs.title: 2.4 RFT-Cosmology-Genesis — exact invariant limit and phenomenological model
docs.text:
Primary source: RFT-Cosmology-Genesis · Exact Invariant Remainder Theorem · Model specification · Results · Limitations.

For the repository's defined normalized invariant,

\[ I_m(\theta)=-16\frac{3^{m-1}+1}{3^{m+1}+3} \sin^2\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right), \]

the exact algebraic limit and finite-level remainder are

\[ I_\infty(\theta)=-\frac{16}{9}\sin^2\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right), \qquad I_m(\theta)-I_\infty(\theta) =-\frac{32}{9(3^m+1)}\sin^2\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right). \]

Its cosmological coupling and CMB response are phenomenological. No physical interaction, observational detection, or agreement with a full CMB likelihood is established.

docs.title: 3. SIRM Core: The Mathematical Foundation
docs.text:
All RFT-SIRM systems are instances of a single deterministic state machine:

State  = (total_supply, total_base_sum, global_field, p, dust_accumulator, base_balance[])

I1: total_supply = total_base_sum + global_field * p
I2: total_supply = total_minted - total_burned
I3: dust_accumulator < p  (when p > 0)
I4: effective_balance[i] >= -(total_supply / 10p)

where effective_balance[i] = base_balance[i] + global_field

Key property: global_field is a scalar. Updating it by Δ changes every participant's effective balance by Δ simultaneously — O(1) regardless of participant count. No iteration. No per-account writes. Deterministic and verifiable.

docs.title: 3.3 Agave Memory Contexts
docs.text:
Property Value Role SVM memory isolation and CPI security research Language Rust Status Active research — bug reported upstream Repository RFT-SIRM/agave-abiv2-memory-contexts Upstream anza-xyz/svm#25 Key Finding CPI permission leakage: per-frame writable permission rollback failure

Problem: During CPI execution in Agave SVM, multiple update_account_permissions calls within a single frame destroyed rollback entries from earlier calls. On pop(), only the last-touched account was restored; earlier accounts retained modified permissions permanently.

Impact: Writable permissions could leak across CPI boundaries, violating isolation guarantees.

Fix: Record each account's pre-frame value only on its first touch within the frame, never overwriting on subsequent calls.

docs.title: 3.4 Agave Scheduler
docs.text:
Property Value Role Conflict-aware transaction scheduling research Language Rust Status RFC published — upstream discussion open Repository RFT-SIRM/agave-rift-scheduler Upstream anza-xyz/agave#14274 Key Finding GreedyScheduler deferred queue lacks retry bound and starvation observability

Observation: GreedyScheduler in Agave defers conflicting transactions by re-inserting them into the priority queue without a per-transaction retry counter, a configurable upper bound, or a dropped_transactions metric.

Impact: Under sustained write contention on a hot account, lower-priority transactions may be deferred indefinitely. They are not lost from the queue, but their scheduling latency is unbounded and unobservable.

Proposal: Add max_retry_count (configurable) and dropped_transactions metric to GreedySchedulerConfig / SchedulingSummary. ~15 lines. No policy change.

Verification: Rift Scheduler reference implementation enforces bounded retry semantics with I1–I4 invariants. 91M+ fuzz executions, 0 violations.

docs.title: Research Programme and Execution Platform
docs.text:
Strategic identity document.

UltraCore-RFT is the coordination hub for a research programme whose public scientific narrative starts with mathematical definitions and evidence: Evgeny's Theory of Everything, the Lean-formalized fourth-moment theorem, and the separate Phi-Genesis spectral audit. The theorem is specific; the broader programme is not claimed to be a completed physical Theory of Everything.

The programme then branches into invariant-based systems engineering and applications. UltraCore's engineering identity remains a deterministic execution architecture—not because the blockchain is the foundation, but because the runtime work is one downstream implementation strand. See the research map and historical development.

docs.title: 1. The Transition
docs.text:
The ecosystem contains two connected but distinct kinds of work: literal mathematical research and systems engineering. The mathematical strand includes a specific fourth-moment identity reported as machine-checked in Lean 4, higher-moment extensions that remain open at the all-level stage, and a separate signed-flux spectral-decimation audit. The systems strand applies invariant-first design to deterministic state transitions, runtimes, protocols, and verification.

The correct hierarchy is therefore not “blockchain first.” It is definitions and theorem → evidence and open questions → engineering methodology → implementations and exploratory applications. The arrows express a reading order and research motivation, not a claim that the theorem proves the applications.

This document explains the execution-platform strand within that larger research programme.

docs.title: 2. What UltraCore Is Not
docs.text: Understanding the platform requires first clearing away mischaracterizations.

docs.title: Not an Operating System
docs.text: An operating system manages hardware resources, process scheduling, device drivers, and user-space interfaces. UltraCore operates at a different layer: it is an execution substrate that coordinates deterministic state transitions across distributed nodes. It can theoretically operate above different verified system kernels — Linux, seL4, or future deterministic kernels — but it does not replace them.

docs.title: Not "Another Blockchain"
docs.text: While the Rift-L1 Blockchain and Rift Network are concrete implementations, the blockchain is one application of the execution architecture, not its defining identity. The same deterministic invariant model can govern validator infrastructure, execution runtimes, distributed systems, and high-assurance computing environments without ever issuing a token or producing a block.

docs.title: Not a Completed Physical Theory of Everything
docs.text: The title of the Evgeny's Theory of Everything repository names a broad research programme; it does not claim that a complete physical theory of the Universe has been proved. The fourth-moment theorem in Evgeny-Theorem is a literal mathematical statement about defined operators and is reported as formalized in Lean 4. The all-level higher-moment recurrence remains open, and Phi-Genesis studies a separate signed-flux operator family. Physical vocabulary used elsewhere in RFT documents remains modelling language unless supported by a separate physical theory and evidence. See Scientific Basis and the AI Guide.

docs.title: 5. Why seL4 Research Matters
docs.text:
The seL4 Capability Derivation Tree (CDT) verification work is frequently misread. This section clarifies its actual role.

What it was: Complementary engineering research. The laboratory explored formally verified kernels to understand deterministic execution environments at the operating-system layer. The goal was methodological — understanding how deterministic invariant systems behave when applied to a formally verified substrate — not architectural.

What it was not: A claim that UltraCore currently runs on seL4, or that seL4 is a dependency of any UltraCore implementation. No production deployment on seL4 exists. No roadmap milestone requires seL4.

What it enables: Three things:

  1. Methodological transferability. The SIRM deterministic verification protocol (seed-controlled fuzzing, invariant telemetry, resource drain verification) was successfully transferred from blockchain runtimes to OS kernels. This demonstrates that the methodology is domain-independent.
  2. Future deployment path. Should a future version of UltraCore Runtime require a formally verified kernel substrate, seL4 represents a known, tested integration point — not a requirement, but an option.
  3. Research credibility. Independent validation of a formally verified system through empirical stress-testing strengthens the laboratory's verification culture. It shows that the team understands both formal methods and empirical methods, and does not conflate them.

See SEL4_CDT_FUZZING.md and seL4 CDT Verification for the full experimental report, including limitations.

docs.title: 6. Research and engineering discipline
docs.text:
The programme contains different evidence types that must not be collapsed into one scorecard. A formal theorem, a finite numerical certificate, a runtime fuzz campaign, a protocol audit, and a kernel stress test answer different questions.

Status policy: use “machine-checked” only for the exact proposition accepted by the proof assistant; “tested” for the assertions actually run; “fuzzed” for the reported campaign; “audited” only for the named review scope; and “open” when a required derivation or validation remains incomplete.

docs.title: 9. Long-term direction
docs.text:
The engineering vision is to explore deterministic, invariant-governed execution in several environments:

docs.title: 2. Mathematical anchor: the fourth-moment identity
docs.text:
For the definitions and assumptions documented by the primary theorem repository,

\[ \Delta_m(H^4,\theta) =\mathrm{Tr}(H_C^4)-\mathrm{Tr}(H_{C'}^4) =-16\left(3^{m-1}+1\right)\sin^2\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right), \qquad m=1,2,3,\ldots. \]

With the source's normalization,

\[ I_m(\theta)=\frac{\Delta_m(H^4,\theta)}{3^{m+1}+3}, \qquad \lim_{m\to\infty}I_m(\theta) =-\frac{16}{9}\sin^2\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right). \]

At the special angle \(\theta=\frac{\pi}{2}\), the limiting value is:

\[ -\frac{8}{9} \]

docs.title: Algebraic sanity checks
docs.text:
• \(3^{m+1}+3=3(3^m+1)\).
  • At \(m=1,\theta=\pi/2\): \(\Delta_1=-16\), dimension \(=12\), and \(I_1=-4/3\).
  • The limit follows by dividing numerator and denominator by \(3^m\).

The source repository reports that the fourth-moment statement is formalized in Lean 4 for the concrete operators and the quantifiers in the formal theorem. A checked formal proposition does not by itself settle independent semantic review, peer review, or novelty relative to the literature.

Primary sources: theorem statement · Lean formalization · verification record.

docs.title: 3. Higher moments: what is and is not closed
docs.text:
The Theory-of-Everything synthesis repository studies \(H^6,H^8,H^{10}\), Fourier coefficients, residuals, and a candidate recurrence.

Supported within the documented finite scope: selected transition coefficients have modular/CRT certificates under explicit construction, denominator, norm, and coefficient-bound arguments; numerical holdouts and sparse-matrix-power checks are also reported.

Still open: proving the all-level recurrence \(R_m^{(p)}(\theta)=R_4^{(p)}(\theta)\) for all \(m\ge3\), all stated admissible angles, and \(p\in\{6,8,10\}\). The exceptional first-transition correction also needs a derivation from the recursive graph/operator structure.

A finite certificate proves its stated finite claim, not an infinite family. Small numerical residuals are evidence, not a universal proof. Read the dissertation, recurrence note, and modular certificate.

docs.title: 4. Phi-Genesis: a separate operator family
docs.text:
Phi-Genesis studies signed \(Z_2\)-flux Laplacians, spectral decimation, boundary/corner corrections, inertia computations, and exploratory mass-index patterns.

  • Gate A remains open while the full exceptional set and residual mismatches are not explained.
  • Tests support only the assertions and inputs actually covered.
  • A selected mass-index pattern is not an established predictive physical law without a mechanism, predeclared predictions, held-out validation, and independent derivation.
  • No equivalence with the SU(2)-connected operators is assumed. A bridge needs an explicit operator map, boundary conditions, preserved quantities, exceptions, and a proof or clearly labelled conjecture.

Keep failed checks and rejected claims in the historical record. They are evidence about the research path, not cosmetic blemishes.

docs.title: 5. SIRM: engineering model and invariants
docs.text:
SIRM specifies runtime constraints for deterministic state transitions. The compact notation below is mapped to implementation variables immediately afterward.

\[ \begin{aligned} I_1:\quad & S = B + Gp,\\ I_2:\quad & S = M - D,\\ I_3:\quad & d < p \quad (p>0),\\ I_4:\quad & E_i \ge -\frac{S}{10p}. \end{aligned} \]

The effective-balance relation is

\[ E_i = b_i + G. \] Symbol Implementation variable \(S\) total_supply \(B\) total_base_sum \(G\) global_field \(M\) total_minted \(D\) total_burned \(d\) dust_accumulator \(E_i\) effective_balance[i] \(b_i\) base_balance[i]

Where \(\mathtt{effective\_balance}[i]=\mathtt{base\_balance}[i]+\mathtt{global\_field}\), under the model's integer and scaling conventions.

The \(O(1)\) distribution argument concerns a shared scalar update and lazy effective-balance calculation. It does not imply every operation is \(O(1)\), nor does the spectral theorem prove the SIRM invariants. Runtime tests, fuzzing, audits, and deployment evidence have implementation-specific scope.

docs.title: 6. Evidence vocabulary
docs.text:
Label Meaning Machine-checked A stated proposition is accepted by the specified proof assistant and build configuration Analytically proved A written proof establishes the statement from explicit assumptions Certified finite-level A certificate covers the stated finite cases under stated bounds Numerically reproduced Computation matches a prediction on named inputs Engineering-tested Tests, fuzzing, audit, or deployment checks support an implementation-specific claim Hypothesis / conjecture A proposed extension awaiting proof or refutation Open A required derivation, proof, independent replication, or experiment is incomplete Rejected / not established Counterexamples or available evidence do not support the stronger claim

A passing workflow proves only the assertions it executes. Fuzz counts and test totals are source-reported snapshots unless the page explicitly implements a live data source.

docs.text:

  3. Higher-moment extension: investigate recurrences and finite-level certificates while keeping the all-level problem open.
  4. Separate signed-flux audit: test spectral-decimation and mass-index claims; preserve failures and unresolved Gate A cases.
  5. Applications: explore runtimes, protocols, kernel stress testing, quantum architecture, and energy-system models without treating them as proofs of the mathematical programme.

This is a conceptual map, not a substitute for commit-backed chronology. Use UltraCore history, theorem history, synthesis history, and Phi-Genesis history for exact dates and changes.

docs.title: Development Strategy
docs.text: Scope: Strategic roadmap, research phases, and ecosystem positioning for the RFT-SIRM deterministic invariant systems laboratory.

docs.title: 1. Mission
docs.text:
Build a deterministic, mathematically verified economic layer for distributed systems where invariants are hard constraints enforced at every state transition.

Core principle: Correctness is not assumed — it is measured, fuzzed, and documented. Every state transition must satisfy the SIRM invariant suite (I1–I4) or be explicitly rejected.

docs.title: 2. Strategic priority: mathematics and evidence first
docs.text: This is a reading order and research map, not a theorem asserting that each downstream application follows from the mathematics. The fourth-moment theorem does not prove the SIRM invariants, the higher-moment recurrence, the Phi-Genesis decimation mechanism, or a quantum advantage. The separate RFT-Cosmology-Genesis repository now records an exact algebraic limit and finite-level remainder for its defined normalized invariant; its cosmological extension remains phenomenological and has no full observational-likelihood validation.

docs.title: Priority I — protect and independently audit the formal theorem
docs.text:
Primary source: Evgeny-Theorem · Lean formalization · theorem statement.

For the specific operator definitions and assumptions in the source repository, the fourth-moment trace defect is stated as

\[ \Delta_m(H^4,\theta) = \mathrm{Tr}(H_C^4)-\mathrm{Tr}(H_{C'}^4) = -16(3^{m-1}+1)\sin^2\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right), \qquad m\ge 1. \]

With the documented normalization,

\[ I_m(\theta) = \frac{\Delta_m(H^4,\theta)}{3^{m+1}+3} \longrightarrow -\frac{16}{9}\sin^2\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right), \qquad I_m\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)\longrightarrow-\frac{8}{9}. \]

docs.title: Closure and maintenance tasks
docs.text:
• Keep the theorem statement, operator definitions, and normalization synchronized with the primary repository; treat that repository as authoritative.
  • Re-run the Lean build from the documented formalization directory after any theorem or dependency change, and report the exact command and result.
  • Independently check the finite-level trace identity against the stated formula, including the boundary cases and the angle convention.
  • Keep the fourth-moment result separate from the higher-moment recurrence: do not describe the all-level recurrence as proved unless its proof is present and verified.
  • Track numerical or spectral-decimation observations as separate evidence; they do not replace the formal theorem's assumptions or proof.

docs.title: Priority II — establish the higher-moment programme
docs.text: Maintain finite-level certificates and numerical cross-checks as evidence, while marking the all-level recurrence as open until a complete proof is available.

docs.title: Priority IV — specify and verify SIRM as an engineering model
docs.text:
SIRM uses four stated runtime constraints. Short symbols are used below to keep the equations robust across GitHub Markdown renderers; the table maps each symbol to the implementation variable.

\[ \begin{aligned} I_1:\quad & S = B + Gp,\\ I_2:\quad & S = M - D,\\ I_3:\quad & d < p \quad (p>0),\\ I_4:\quad & E_i \ge -\frac{S}{10p}. \end{aligned} \]

The effective-balance relation is

\[ E_i = b_i + G. \] Symbol Implementation variable \(S\) total_supply \(B\) total_base_sum \(G\) global_field \(M\) total_minted \(D\) total_burned \(d\) dust_accumulator \(E_i\) effective_balance[i] \(b_i\) base_balance[i]

Assess Rift-L1, Rift-Network, scheduler, memory-context, and exploratory application tracks using their own tests, audits, benchmarks, and deployment criteria. Do not infer production readiness or quantum advantage from the mathematical results above.
3. The RFT Methodology
docs.text:
RFT-SIRM operates as a multi-stage research pipeline. Each stage feeds into the next, but stages are independent enough to be evaluated, funded, and deployed separately.

│   Stage 0       │ --> │   Stage 1       │ --> │   Stage 2       │
│  Mathematical   │     │  Reference      │     │  Protocol       │
│  Foundation     │     │  Implementation │     │  Deployment     │
